goal: Iske baad aap function prototype likh sakte hain, bata sakte hain ke main ke baad define hone wale function ke liye iski zaroorat kyun parti hai, aur declaration aur definition mein farq bata sakte hain.
warmup: Ek teacher attendance list upar se neeche parhti hai. Agar list mein likha ho 'Ali, jisay sports captain ne bulaya' lekin woh abhi tak kisi sports captain se mili hi nahi, to woh confuse ho jati hai. Agar pehle page par likha ho 'Sports captain: Bilal', to usay baad mein pata hota hai ke kaun hai. Prototype woh pehla page hai: yeh function ko use hone se pehle compiler se mutaarif karwata hai.
definition: Compiler aap ka program upar se neeche parhta hai. Agar main() koi aisa function call kare jo main ke NEECHE likha ho, to compiler abhi us se mila hi nahi hota aur error de deta hai. Function prototype (jisay function declaration bhi kehte hain) is masle ko hal karta hai. Yeh function ka header hota hai jis ke baad semicolon hota hai, body nahi hoti. Yeh compiler ko function ka naam, return type aur parameter types pehle se bata deta hai. Definition poora function hota hai body { } ke saath, aur woh baad mein, yahan tak ke main ke baad bhi, aa sakti hai.
howItWorks: Pipeline dekhein. Pehle compiler upar likhe prototypes parhta hai. Phir woh main() parhta hai, aur jab circleArea(3) dekhta hai to usay pehle se pata hota hai ke yeh function maujood hai aur usay kya chahiye, is liye error nahi aata. Asli code aage neeche mil jata hai. Prototype aur uski definition function ke naam, return type, aur parameters ki ginti aur types par bilkul agree karni chahiye. Prototype mein parameter ke naam optional hain: int add(int, int); utna hi valid hai jitna int add(int a, int b);. Definition mein naam hone zaroori hain (woh unhein use karti hai). Teachers yeh layout pasand karte hain: upar prototypes, phir main() taake asal idea asani se mil jaye, phir neeche definitions. Prototype ke baad semicolon na bhoolein. Yahi usay declaration banata hai, warna woh bina body ka function header ban jata hai.
